RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Taylor Alvarez
Member ID: W131874845
Reference Number: POC-CA1D31244E-60243
Date of Notice: 2026-08-05
Requested Service: Partial knee replacement, CPT 27446

To Whom It May Concern:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for partial (unicompartmental) knee replacement, CPT 27446, as communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-05 (Reference No. POC-CA1D31244E-60243). The stated reason for denial was that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery."

I respectfully disagree with this determination. I want to note for the record that I have not been provided with the specific written medical policy or clinical criteria document the plan applied in reaching this decision — the denial notice references only "the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria" without naming, numbering, dating, or attaching that document. Because I have not seen that document, I am not able to quote it, and nothing in quotation marks below should be understood as language from the plan's policy. I am formally requesting, as part of this appeal, that the plan provide a copy of the specific medical-necessity criteria, guideline, or clinical policy (including title, policy number, and effective date) that was applied to CPT 27446 in my case, as I understand I am entitled to receive under applicable Medicaid managed care regulations.

Notwithstanding that the specific criteria have not been disclosed to me, the clinical record submitted with the original prior authorization request in fact documents an extensive and adequate trial of conservative (non-surgical) management, as summarized below:

1. Duration and severity of symptoms: I have had 14 months of progressive knee pain that has not been relieved by rest, indicating a chronic, worsening condition rather than an acute or self-limited one.

2. Structured physical therapy: I completed a full course of supervised physical therapy — 16 visits over 8 weeks (2026-05-17 through 2026-07-12) — focused on quadriceps strengthening and range-of-motion restoration. This course of therapy was completed and is documented in the physical therapy discharge note, not abandoned prematurely.

3. Medication trial: I was treated with NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief of pain.

4. Injection therapy: I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-21, which produced only approximately 4 weeks of partial relief before symptoms returned.

5. Objective imaging findings: MRI of the knee on 2026-06-15 demonstrated full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes medially — objective, severe, unicompartmental structural disease consistent with the requested unicompartmental (partial) knee arthroplasty.

6. Functional impairment: I am currently unable to climb stairs without assistance and wake 3-4 times nightly due to pain, reflecting a significant, ongoing impact on activities of daily living and sleep despite the conservative measures above.

7. Physical examination: Exam findings include positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain, corroborating the imaging findings and functional limitations.

8. Absence of contraindications: There is no active infection and no untreated substance use disorder. My BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker, none of which present a barrier to surgery.

Taken together, this record reflects more than four months of combined conservative treatment (medication, injection, and a completed structured physical therapy program) without adequate or durable relief, in the setting of severe, imaging-confirmed, single-compartment degenerative joint disease and significant functional impairment. I believe this record satisfies any reasonable conservative-treatment requirement for consideration of unicompartmental knee arthroplasty, and I ask that the denial be reversed.

My surgeon, Dr. Duval, MD (orthopedic surgery), is available to provide any additional clinical information, peer-to-peer discussion, or documentation the plan requires to complete this appeal. Please contact [Dr. Duval's office / contact information — not stated in the records provided] to arrange this if needed.

I am submitting this appeal within the time frame stated in the denial notice (180 days from 2026-08-05, i.e., by 2027-02-01). However, because standard Medicaid managed care rules generally require plan-level appeals to be filed within a shorter window, I am submitting this appeal now, promptly upon receipt of the denial, to ensure it is timely under whichever deadline applies. Please confirm receipt of this appeal in writing and advise if any additional deadline applies to my case.

I request:
1. Reversal of the denial and authorization of CPT 27446 (partial knee replacement) as requested by Dr. Duval.
2. A copy of the specific medical policy/clinical criteria document applied to this determination, including its title, policy number, and effective date.
3. Written confirmation of receipt of this appeal and the applicable decision timeframe.
4. If this appeal is denied, information on the next level of appeal available to me, including a Medicaid Fair Hearing before the Florida Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA), and my continued right to benefits pending appeal where applicable.

Please contact me at [Phone Number] or [Email Address] with any questions or if additional documentation is needed.

Sincerely,

Taylor Alvarez
Member ID: W131874845

Enclosures:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-17 to 2026-07-12)
- Medication and injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection 2026-04-21)
- MRI report, 2026-06-15
- Clinic/exam notes documenting functional limitations and provocative testing
- [Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Duval, if available — not stated in the records provided]
